title: Food security
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:43Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-food-security-means, covers only availability and access, while the new brief also requires food to be used well (safe, nutritious) and to stay steady over time, so adding those would change what the card teaches rather than make a small adjustment.

draft.title: Food security
card: Food security means everyone has reliable access to enough safe and nutritious food. It is about people, not only about how much food a country grows.
Food must be available: enough is grown, imported or stored. It must also be affordable, so people can buy it with the money they have.
People need to use food well. That means safe food, clean water to prepare it, and a diet with enough nutrients.
Food must be steady over time. Access that is lost in a drought, a war or a price spike is not secure.
draft.remember: Food security needs food that is available, affordable, used well and steady.

a.q: A country grows more than enough grain, but prices are so high that many families cannot buy it. Which part of food security is failing?
a.why: Plenty of grain is grown, so food is available. Families cannot pay for it, so it is not affordable. Availability is the tempting wrong answer, but it is about whether enough food exists, not whether people can buy it.
a.clue: The food exists, but can people pay for it?

b.q: Village A has plenty of cheap rice all year, but its only water source is contaminated, and children often fall ill after meals. Which statement is correct?
opts: Food is available and affordable, but not used well
Food is affordable and used well, but not available
Food is secure, because there is plenty of cheap rice
Food is available, but not affordable or steady
b.why: Rice is plentiful and cheap, so it is available and affordable. Contaminated water means the food is not prepared or used safely, so food security is still not met. Calling it secure is tempting, but having cheap food is only part of the idea.
b.clue: Think about what happens to the rice before it is eaten.

b.best: Food is available and affordable, but not used well
